model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: a D+14 seat, a long-serving incumbent, and a massive financial edge over a Republican challenger who has raised only about $53K and has under $1,000 on hand. Markets price Sherman at roughly 96%, consistent with a Safe D rating.

overview:
Brad Sherman, a Democrat, seeks another term in a Los Angeles-area House district that leans about 14 points Democratic. He advanced to the general election as the incumbent and holds a decisive financial advantage, with roughly $2.7 million on hand after raising over $2.5 million, plus outside groups supporting him. Republican Larry Thompson has raised about $53,000 and reports under $1,000 in cash, with no outside spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the forecast rests on district partisanship, incumbency, and money. Prediction markets give Sherman about a 96% chance of winning. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with an expected margin of roughly 22 points.
